summary: Maine Forest Service steel lookout on Rocky Mountain in the North Woods; its cab was blown off in a 2017 windstorm and the steel tower still stands.

facts.design: Guyed steel tower with an 8 by 8 foot wooden cab, reached by an open ladder (NHLR)
facts.status_note: The steel tower still stands, but its cab was blown off in 2017.

access.note: Access is by permit over private timber roads from the Dickey checkpoint; the summit is reached only by trail.

events.note: Log station built by landowners before the fire district was created
Wooden tower 20 feet high on the south bluff, per Chief Warden Buck; a 1919 report describes a log tower on another bluff instead
Steel tower: the register gives 54 feet with an 8 by 8 foot wooden cab; a 1920 inventory and a 1921 newspaper item give 48 feet
Registered November 24, 1995; nominated by Robert Spear, FFLA
Cab blown off the steel tower in a windstorm on October 30, 2017

notes_for_editor: Height: register says 54 ft (16.5 m); the 1920 inventory and 1921 newspaper item say 48 ft (14.6 m). The record's 14.6 m is kept; the conflict is unresolved. Early history: a 1917 wooden tower (warden report) conflicts with a 1919 report of a log tower on another bluff; unresolved. The 2017 cab loss is confirmed by two sources. The FFLA list marks the tower Standing*, and its footnote defines that mark as a tower whose structure stands with the cab no longer in place; the steel tower's standing rests on that list, and the cab loss on the 2017 report and Forest Lookouts. Access is by permit from private timber roads; no permit contact or trail details were verified. Ownership: the register places it in the Maine North Woods with 7 Island Land Co. named; the owner is not stated.
